[Section] Mix-Source Approach
[source_id=39] Another data augmentation method considered useful in this low-resourced setting is the mix-source method BIBREF12 . In this method, we can utilize the monolingual data of the target language in a multilingual NMT system by mixing the original source sentences with those target monolingual data. The multilingual framework then uses the share information across source and target languages to improve the decision of the target words to be chosen.
[source_id=40] Specifically, there are a small parallel corpus INLINEFORM0 of the language pair X-Y which has INLINEFORM1 sentence pairs INLINEFORM2 ( INLINEFORM3 ) and a big monolingual corpus INLINEFORM4 of the language Y which has INLINEFORM5 sentences INLINEFORM6 ( INLINEFORM7 , INLINEFORM8 ). Now from the monolingual corpus INLINEFORM9 we can generate a parallel corpus INLINEFORM10 where we try to model the identical translation Y-Y: INLINEFORM11 ( INLINEFORM12 ). Then we mix INLINEFORM13 and INLINEFORM14 to get a parallel corpus of the size INLINEFORM15 . Similar to the Back Translation, we subsample INLINEFORM16 Vietnamese sentence pairs from the corpus INLINEFORM17 then the size of the parallel data we have is also doubled.
[source_id=41] To let the NMT knows which language a certain source sentence is in and then can model the language information, we follows the conventions from BIBREF12 . We append language tags to every word in both source and target sentences of the mixed INLINEFORM0 corpus to indicate the language of the words. This technique shows the effectiveness in low-resourced scenarios BIBREF13 , BIBREF14 and our Japanese INLINEFORM1 Vietnamese is such a scenario.
